name: sigh-look
story: Standing in profile, her hand resting on the lower front of her bump, at the top of a deep breath, eyes closed. She lets it out in a long slow sigh, opens her eyes onto her bump and settles, calm, looking down at it. Ends on a held pose (a clip for the Braxton Hicks story: a tightening has passed).
intensity: very gentle and calm, an unhurried mindful moment. Small, soft moves; nothing fast, nothing big.
handsBoxNote: film px holding the hand on her bump all shot: blind_ab.py and critic_F.py draw it at 1:1 and its motion per second (lesson 58)
note: A re-cut of breathe-stroke (Braxton Hicks story, direction A): its sigh (4.85 s on) into its look down onto the bump (7.4–7.85 s), then a hold; face-calm's resting mouth instead of the smile, no stroke. Same keys, reach, breath and life as breathe-stroke; the sigh's long settle tail (6.3–7.4 s there) is shortened by 0.85 s.
